# Best Gravity Forms Copper CRM Integration tools in 2026

## Direct Answer

You can **connect Gravity Forms to Copper CRM** in three ways. All three need a Copper plan with API access (trial, Professional, or Business; Basic will not work). Pick what you need:

- **Outfunnel:** best for contact matching, web tracking, and lead scoring. Billed monthly by active contacts.
- **Gravity Extra:** best for one dedicated form-to-Copper connection. One-time purchase, priced by site.
- **Bit Integrations:** best for multiple Copper record types or wider WordPress automation. It doesn’t just connect Gravity Forms with Copper CRM, it also lets you build **unlimited integrations and automation flows** between more than hundreds of apps without requiring extra add-ons, per-integration fees, or coding. Annual or lifetime license available, priced by site.







If your business relies on **Gravity Forms** to collect leads and **Copper CRM** to manage customer relationships, connecting the two can eliminate hours of manual data entry while ensuring every lead reaches your sales team instantly. Whether you’re capturing contact requests, demo bookings, or support inquiries, a reliable integration keeps your CRM updated automatically and reduces the risk of missed opportunities.

While there are several ways to connect Gravity Forms with Copper CRM, not every solution offers the same balance of features, flexibility, and pricing. Some tools focus solely on syncing Gravity Forms with Copper, while others provide a broader automation platform that [**can connect hundreds of apps**](https://bit-integrations.com/blog/integrate-gravity-forms-without-upgrading-plan/) and workflows from a single dashboard.

In this guide, we’ll compare three of the best Gravity Forms Copper CRM integration tools in 2026—**Outfunnel**, **Gravity Extra**, and **Bit Integrations**—breaking down their features, pricing, ease of use, and which type of user each solution is best suited for.

## The Copper plan requirement (read this once)

**All three methods depend on Copper features that are gated by plan.** Copper documents Developer API access on its trial, Professional, and Business plans.

The free trial grants temporary access to Professional and Business-level features, including the API, which is how this article’s Bit Integrations test ran on a Business-plan trial.

Copper Basic and Starter do not include API access. Copper separately lists the Outfunnel connector as available on Professional and Business only.

**Buying Outfunnel, Gravity Extra, or Bit Integrations does not add the integration to a Copper Basic account.** Because this rule governs every method below, it is stated here once instead of being repeated in each section.

***Sources*** ***from******:*** [Copper plan comparison](https://support.copper.com/en/articles/9623758-copper-plans-feature-comparison) | [Copper API documentation](https://support.copper.com/en/articles/8823462-api-docs-and-tips) | [Copper Gravity Forms listing](https://www.copper.com/integrations/gravity-forms)

## Let’s compare the three methods

This table compares the methods by plan eligibility, payment model, supported record types, conditional logic, tracking, and best fit.

Gravity Extra is a purpose-built connector for one job. **Bit Integrations supports more Copper action types** and a broader WordPress automation stack.

## Method 1: The Copper marketplace integration by Outfunnel

### Is this a native Copper integration?

No. Copper lists the Gravity Forms connector in its marketplace, but the page labels it “Integration by Outfunnel” and sends users to Outfunnel for support. Copper approves and surfaces the integration; Outfunnel develops, operates, and bills for it.

![Copper CRM Marketplace](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Copper-CRM-Marketpalace-1024x457.webp)    ### How the Outfunnel integration works

When someone submits a Gravity Form, Outfunnel creates a contact in Copper. If a contact with the same email address already exists, Outfunnel records the new submission against that contact rather than creating a duplicate.

Outfunnel documents these additional capabilities:

- Map form fields to Copper fields.
- Log form submissions on Copper contact timelines.
- Show sync status and problems that block a record from syncing.
- Capture landing-page, referrer, and UTM details.
- Track website visits before and after a submission.
- Calculate lead scores.

These features make Outfunnel more than a form-to-CRM connector. They add marketing and website context that helps a sales team see where a lead came from and what the lead did after submitting.

### Outfunnel pricing

Outfunnel is billed separately from Copper. Its pricing page showed these starting prices when reviewed:

- Basic: from $59 per month for 500 active contacts.
- Professional: from $99 per month for 1,000 active contacts.
- Scale: from $299 per month for 15,000 or more active contacts, billed annually.

An active contact is counted when the person is part of an active sync, has email or web engagement recorded, visits the tracked website, or receives a lead score during the billing period. The tier you need depends on activity, not on the total number of records stored in Copper.

***Sources:*** [Copper marketplace listing](https://www.copper.com/integrations/gravity-forms) | [Outfunnel integration page](https://outfunnel.com/copper-gravity-forms-integration/) | [Outfunnel pricing](https://outfunnel.com/pricing/)

## Method 2: The Gravity Extra Copper CRM add-on

Gravity Extra sells a WordPress add-on built specifically to connect Gravity Forms with Copper CRM. It runs on the WordPress site, connects through Copper’s API, and uses one-time site-based pricing instead of active-contact pricing.

### **What the Gravity Extra add-on supports**

According to its product documentation, the add-on can:

- Connect Gravity Forms with Copper through the API.
- Create multiple feeds.
- Select a target Copper module.
- Map standard and custom fields.
- Apply conditional logic.
- Process matching submissions automatically.

This is a focused connector, not a general automation platform.

### **Gravity Extra pricing**

The product page showed these one-time promotional prices when reviewed in July 2026:

**License****Displayed price****Regular price shown****1 site**$29$49**5 sites**$59$129**10 sites**$129$229The vendor describes the purchase as a one-time payment. Promotional prices and support terms change, so confirm the checkout page before buying.

***Sources:*** [Gravity Extra product page](https://gravityextra.com/gravity-forms-copper-crm-integration-premium-add-on/) | [Gravity Extra documentation](https://gravityextra.com/docs/gravity-forms-copper-crm-integration-premium-add-on/)

## Method 3: Bit Integrations – Most Affordable with Higher Possibilities 

Bit Integrations runs entirely inside the **WordPress dashboard**, so no external server sits between the form and Copper. When a visitor submits the connected Gravity Form, the plugin sends the **mapped data to Copper’s API** and creates the record type you selected: a Company, Person, Opportunity, or Task.

A **visual field-mapping** panel pairs each form field with a Copper field, and you can map more fields, including Copper custom fields, by adding rows.

Beyond the core mapping, the Copper action supports:

- Assigning an owner to the new record with the Add Owner option.
- Adding the record to a company and applying tags during creation.
- Conditional logic, so a submission reaches Copper only when it meets rules you set, for example, a specific country or plan selection.
- Custom values and webhooks for more advanced routing.
- A per-integration timeline that logs each run as a success or error for troubleshooting.

Because Bit Integrations authorizes with a **Copper account email and API key**, it needs a Copper plan that includes API access. It does not add its own web tracking, lead scoring, or attribution, which remain Outfunnel’s strengths.

The same Copper action also works with [WPForms](https://bit-integrations.com/free-wpforms-integration-with-hundreds-of-platforms/), [Contact Form 7](https://bit-integrations.com/free-contact-form-7-integration/), [Bit Form](https://bit-integrations.com/free-bit-form-integrations/), [Elementor](https://bit-integrations.com/free-elementor-form-integration/), and [WooCommerce](https://bit-integrations.com/integrate-woocommerce-plugin-for-free/). For the wider picture, see how to [integrate Gravity Forms without upgrading your plan](https://bit-integrations.com/blog/integrate-gravity-forms-without-upgrading-plan/).

Bit Integrations also supports other WordPress triggers and more than hundreds of external destinations, from [sending Gravity Forms entries to Google Sheets](https://bit-integrations.com/blog/connect-gravity-forms-to-google-sheets/) to [Gravity Forms email marketing integrations](https://bit-integrations.com/blog/gravity-forms-email-marketing-integrations/), so it doubles as a general automation layer for the site.

## Which method should you choose?

There is no single right answer for every team. Match the method to the outcome you need:

- **Choose Outfunnel** when you want contacts matched by email, submissions logged on Copper timelines, and website visits or lead scores added to the CRM.
- **Choose Gravity Extra** when you want one dedicated connection for this single workflow and prefer a one-time, site-based purchase.
- **Choose Bit Integrations** when you need to create **People/Contact, Companies, Opportunities, or Tasks**, or when you expect to connect other WordPress plugins and services later.

### The connector price is not the total cost

The connector is only one line on the invoice. The Outfunnel route needs an eligible Copper Professional or Business subscription plus a separate Outfunnel subscription.

Gravity Extra and Bit Integrations skip Outfunnel but still need Copper API access, which is limited to the trial, professional, and business plans. For teams with several Copper users, the CRM subscription can cost more than the connector itself.

## How to connect Gravity Forms to Copper CRM with Bit Integrations Step-by-step guide

We tested the workflow below using fictional form data.

**Test item****Configuration****WordPress trigger**Gravity Forms submission**Copper action**Create Person**Copper account**Business-plan trial**Authentication**Copper account email and API key**Result**Person created successfully and verified in Copper**Scope of this test**  
The test covers a “Create Person” workflow. It does not test **duplicate updating**, Create Opportunity, Create Task, retry behavior, or every field type.

### Test form fields

The Gravity Form contained these fields: First name, Last name, Username, Email, Country, Phone number, Postal code, City, Region, Message, Subject, and Attachment. Only the fields selected in the Bit Integrations field map were sent to Copper.



### Step 1: Create a new Bit Integrations workflow

Install and activate **[Bit Integrations](https://wordpress.org/plugins/bit-integrations/)** on the same WordPress site that runs Gravity Forms. Open Bit Integrations from the WordPress dashboard and select Create Integration.

![Install and activate Bit Integrations](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Install-and-acitvate-Bit-Integrations-1024x513.webp)    ### Step 2: Select Gravity Forms as the trigger

Search for Gravity Forms on the trigger screen and select it.

![Gravity Forms Integration with Bit Integrations - Search and Select Gravity Forms](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Gravity-Forms-Integration-with-Bit-Integrations-Search-and-Select-Gravity-Forms-1024x440.png)    ### Step 3: Choose the Gravity Form

Open the form dropdown and choose the form that should send data to Copper CRM. In this test, the selected form was named “Gravity Forms Integrations.” Click Next.

![Choose Specific Forms created with Gravity forms](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Choose-Specefic-Forms-created-with-Gravity-forms.webp)    ### Step 4: Select Copper CRM as the action

Search for Copper CRM on the action screen and select the Copper CRM card.

![Search and select Copper CRM as an action](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Search-and-select-Copper-CRM-as-an-action-1024x505.webp)    ### Step 5: Enter the Copper API credentials

Bit Integrations needs the **email address** tied to the Copper account and a **Copper API key**. Enter both values and click Authorize. The Next button becomes available after successful authorization.

![Authorize Copper using API](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Authorize-Copper-using-API-1024x519.webp)    **Security note**  
Treat the API key like a password. Do not expose it in a public screenshot, video, support ticket, or shared document.

**Don’t know how to find the Copper API key? Just follow these steps:**

In Copper, open the account menu in the upper-left corner and select Customization.

![Go to Copper CRM customization](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Go-to-Copper-CRM-customization-1024x486.webp)    In the Copper settings sidebar, find the Integrations section and **select API Keys**. An administrator may be required to access or generate API credentials, and Copper limits API availability by plan.

![Click on API keys](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Click-on-API-keys-1024x515.webp)    Click Generate API Key. Copper creates a key and shows it in the API Key column. **Add a clear label** so the purpose is easy to identify later, such as “**WordPress Gravity Forms Integration.**”

Copy the key and return to Bit Integrations. Do not reuse the key in unrelated tools, and revoke it if it is ever exposed.

![Click on Generate API key](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Click-on-Generate-API-key-1024x514.webp)    ### Step 6: Select Create Person and map the fields

After authorization, select **Create Person from the action dropdown**. The goal of this test was to turn each qualifying Gravity Forms submission into a new Person record in Copper.

Now map the fields, First name to Name, Message to Description, Email to Email, City to City, and Postal code to Postal Code. The Add Company, Add Tags, and Add Owner utilities were turned on, and conditional logic was available but left off.

The remaining fields, Username, Country, Region, Subject, and Attachment, were not mapped, so they did not appear in the resulting record. After reviewing the mapping, click Next and save the integration.

![Select Create Person and map the fields](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Map-the-fields-1-1024x536.webp)    ### Step 7: Submit a test entry

Open the form on the website and submit fictional test data. Testing with **non-sensitive information** confirms the mapping without adding a real customer to the CRM.

![Submit a test Gravity form](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Submit-a-test-form.webp)    ### Step 8: Check the Bit Integrations log

Open the integration timeline after submitting the form. The test log returned Status: Success, Record type: Person, and the response “Person created successfully.”

The timeline helps identify authorization, mapping, or API problems, but a successful API response should still be followed by a manual check in Copper.

![Integration log](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Integration-log-1024x500.webp)    ### Step 9: Verify the Person in Copper CRM

Open People in Copper and locate the new record. The test confirmed that Copper received the mapped name and email, as well as the selected company and owner.

The Gravity Forms trigger, Create Person action, field mapping, company assignment, owner assignment, and success log all worked in the tested environment.

![Person created at Copper CRM](https://bit-integrations.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Person-created-at-Copper-CRM-1024x516.webp)    ## What the test confirmed

- Only mapped fields reached Copper.
- Mapping only the first name produced a first-name-only Person record.
- The Company and Owner utilities populated the related Copper fields.
- Bit Integrations recorded the API response in its WordPress timeline.
- A successful log still needed a final manual check inside Copper.
- The test verified record creation, not duplicate-contact updating.

## Common setup mistakes

Five errors account for most failed or messy setups:

- **Assuming Copper Basic includes API access.** Confirm the account plan before buying a connector; see the plan requirement above.
- **Publishing a partial API key in a screenshot.** Blur the entire key, not part of it. A visible key can expose CRM data.
- **Mapping only the first name.** Copper requires a Name value for a Person, so map a complete name whenever possible.
- **Mapping every form field by default.** Send only the information the sales team uses. Extra data clutters records and adds privacy risk.
- **Skipping the final Copper check.** A successful response means Copper accepted the request, not that every field landed in the right place. Test with fictional data first.

## Final recommendation

No method wins for every Copper user. **Outfunnel** fits when contact matching, website tracking, attribution, lead scoring, and submission history sit at the center of the sales process, provided the separate Outfunnel bill is acceptable.

**Gravity Extra** fits a site that needs one dedicated connection at a one-time cost. **Bit Integrations** fits sites that need several Copper record types or broader automation.

Before you commit, confirm three things:

1. Your Copper plan includes the required integration or API access.
2. The connector supports the Copper record type and behavior you need.
3. The full cost fits your number of Copper users, WordPress sites, and active contacts.

Then submit fictional test data and verify both the integration log and the final Copper record before you send real leads.

## Frequently Asked Questions about Gravity Forms Copper CRM integration

### **Does Copper include a Gravity Forms integration?**

Copper lists the Gravity Forms integration in its marketplace, but Outfunnel develops and supports it. Copper Professional and Business plans can use the connector; the Outfunnel account and subscription are separate and are not included in the Copper price.





### Which integration is the most affordable?

Bit Integrations is the most affordable overall, starting at $35 per year with unlimited integrations and flows. Gravity Extra can be suitable for a single dedicated connection, while Outfunnel starts at $29 per month and becomes more expensive as your active contact count increases.





### Are there limits on integrations or automation flows?

Yes, depending on the tool. Outfunnel limits usage based on active contacts, while Gravity Extra focuses on individual add-ons and feeds. Bit Integrations allows unlimited integrations and automation flows without extra per-flow charges.





### Can these tools create contacts and leads in Copper CRM?

Yes. Outfunnel can create and update contacts, while Gravity Extra supports records such as people, leads, and tasks. Bit Integrations can create people, companies, opportunities, and tasks in Copper CRM from Gravity Forms submissions.





### Does Bit Integrations only connect Gravity Forms with Copper CRM?

No. Bit Integrations is not limited to a single connection. It can connect Gravity Forms, Copper CRM, and many other WordPress plugins, CRMs, marketing platforms, spreadsheets, and business tools from the same WordPress dashboard.





### Do I need to buy additional add-ons for Bit Integrations?

Bit Integrations is designed to provide multiple integrations within one platform. This means you generally do not need to purchase a separate add-on each time you want to connect another supported app or WordPress plugin





### Do I need to buy additional add-ons for Bit Integrations while connecting Gravity Forms to Copper CRM?

Bit Integrations is designed to provide multiple integrations within one platform. This means you do not need to purchase a separate add-on if you want to connect another supported app or WordPress plugin.





### **Can I map Gravity Forms fields to Copper custom fields in Bit Integrations?**

Yes. The mapping panel lists Copper’s standard fields, and custom fields appear alongside them once they exist in Copper. Add rows to map more pairs. Create the Copper custom field first, since the panel can only target fields that already exist.





### **Which Copper user is the API key tied to, and does it need admin access?**

The key is user-scoped. Every record the integration creates is attributed to the key’s owner in Copper’s audit log, so choose that user deliberately. Keys are generated under Settings, then Integrations, then API Keys, which usually requires an administrator.





### **What credentials does the integration send to Copper?**

Copper’s API authenticates with a pair of values: the API key and the email address of the user who owns that key. Both are required, and a wrong or missing value returns an authorization error. That is why Bit Integrations asks for the account email as well as the key.





### **Are there Copper API rate limits that could affect a busy form?**

Copper enforces per-key rate limits and returns an HTTP 429 response when they are exceeded. Recent developer guides cite roughly 600 requests per minute per key, with bulk endpoints limited further, though published figures vary, so check Copper’s developer documentation for the current number. Ordinary form-submission volume stays well below any of these limits.
